newsitem.title: JAPAN: JCR downgrades Bank of Osaka"s debt rating to BB.
newsitem.headline: JCR downgrades Bank of Osaka"s debt rating to BB.

text.p: Japan Credit Rating Agency Ltd (JCR) said on Tuesday it had downgraded its long-term debt rating for Bank of Osaka Ltd to BB from BBB-.
The rating is currently JCR"s lowest for any Japanese bank.
By JCR"s rating standard, ratings above BBB- are "investment grade" and those below "BB+" are described as "speculative grade".
The decision affects 10 billion yen worth of convertible bonds that will mature on March 31. They were issued in 1988.

The rating agency attributed the downgrade to its expectation that it would not be easy for the Bank of Osaka to write off all its non-performing debts in view of its expected future operating profits, its current capital and its current loan loss reserves.
But JCR also said it expects the bank to receive support from the Japanese authorities.
